title: Single-exponential exact cut mimicking networks
formal: Does there exist an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that every finite undirected graph \(G\) with nonnegative real edge weights and a specified terminal set \(T\) of size \(k\ge2\) has an undirected nonnegatively real-weighted graph \(H\) containing the same labelled terminals, with \(|V(H)|\le2^{Ck}\), that preserves every minimum terminal bipartition cut value exactly?
definitions: Graphs are finite and simple, with finite edge weights. For every nonempty proper subset \(A\subset T\), define \(\lambda_{G}(A)=\min\{\sum_{e\in\delta_{G}(S)}w_{e}:S\subseteq V(G),\ S\cap T=A\}\), where \(\delta_{G}(S)\) is the set of edges with exactly one endpoint in \(S\). Define \(\lambda_{H}\) in the same way, using the weights of \(H\). Preservation means \(\lambda_{H}(A)=\lambda_{G}(A)\) simultaneously for every such \(A\). New nonterminal vertices and arbitrary nonnegative real weights are allowed; \(H\) need not be a subgraph, minor or contraction of \(G\). Its vertex bound includes the terminals. The constant is independent of \(G\), its weights and \(k\). No algorithm or construction-time bound is requested.

context_blocks.text: A terminal cut function records how expensive it is to separate any chosen group of terminals from all the others. An exact mimicking network stores this whole function as a smaller graph.
For general graphs, the reviewed size gap is \(2^{\Omega(k)}\) versus \(2^{2^{O(k)}}\). Chen and Tan review this gap and improve bounds for special graph classes.
Requiring a contraction would change the answer: doubly exponential lower bounds are known in that restricted representation. The question permits an arbitrary replacement graph.

A Gomory–Hu tree preserves pairwise minimum cuts. A terminal bipartition constrains many vertices to each side simultaneously, so pairwise cut preservation does not establish this stronger representation property.

why: Resolving the exponential-versus-doubly-exponential gap would determine how compactly an arbitrary network can represent all exact terminal separation costs.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the specified model, quantifiers and guarantees. A conditional lower bound settles only its conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean; a partial improvement does not meet the target.

progress.text: General exact mimicking networks have size bounded only by the number of terminals, with a doubly exponential upper bound.
The general gap remains in the reviewed bounds; improved special-class results and contraction lower bounds refine the landscape.

status_note: Sources and subsequent-result searches checked on 13 September 2026. The cited results leave this target unanswered; this is a bounded literature review, not an exhaustive certification of current openness. Editorial linear-exponent endpoint: the precise target is 2 to a constant times k, not an unspecified exponential in a polynomial of k. Arbitrary replacement graphs and exact set-cut preservation are essential.

sentences: An exact cut mimicking network represents every minimum cut separating a group of terminals from its complement.
It must preserve all terminal bipartition values simultaneously.
The question asks whether every weighted undirected graph has such a representation with singly exponential size in the number of terminals.
Arbitrary new nonterminal vertices are permitted, with no restriction to contractions.
The general gap between exponential lower bounds and doubly exponential upper bounds remains the target.
